mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2.5%) compresses discount rates and stimulates equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% signals economic weakness that triggers a sell-off in equities, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 4.0% in 20% of the sample and 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: Strong housing demand (HOUST > 1200 thousand units) combined with weak industrial production (INDPRO < 100) signals an economic imbalance that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST > 1200 and INDPRO < 100, 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), the Federal Reserve's policy rate hikes dampen economic growth and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 4.0% in 20% of the sample and 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: Strong housing starts (HOUST > 1200 thousand units) consistently signal robust consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST > 1200 in 20% of the sample and 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) signals the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 3.0% in 20% of the sample and 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly) supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly in 20% of the sample and 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: Strong consumer credit demand (RSAFS > 500,000 million dollars) combined with low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2.5%) fuels consumer spending and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary accommodation and strong consumer demand
failure_condition: When RSAFS > 500,000 and FEDFUNDS < 2.5%, 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances.
